3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: It was a rainy day in Kyrute, one of only a handful the island experienced per year.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: The sound of the falling drops on the Alliance of Nations dome made for an unexpectedly soothing backdrop to what I could tell was going to be a tense session.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: I sat with Laurento and the rest of the Rizian delegation in the half-full assembly hall.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: Today's session was to focus on South Merkopa only. Looking around the room, I could see representatives and leaders from Wehlen, Morella, Derdia and Lespia.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: Duke Axel Reinhart entered late, accompanied by a few of his ministers. He took a seat as far from the Lespian delegation as possible.

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: Duke Axel Reinhart and Patricio Alvarez entered late, deep in conversation. They nodded at each other and took seats with their respective delegations.

15.speaker: Narrator
15.text: Duke Axel Reinhart and Patricio Alvarez entered late, deep in conversation. They nodded at each other and took seats with their respective delegations.
15.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Buy"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLCSupport.Journal_Turn04_Pales_EndGasDeal"] == true) == false)

16.speaker: Player_Romus
16.text: "Alvarez must have given him quite the talking-to."

17.speaker: Player_Romus
17.text: "It must be awkward, encountering one's ex-husband here."

18.speaker: Player_Romus
18.text: "I wonder how badly the two of them fell out."

20.speaker: Player_Romus
20.text: "I wonder what they were talking about."

21.speaker: Player_Romus
21.text: "Did I make a mistake? Should I have gone with the Duke's deal after all?"

22.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
22.text: "They clearly plan to put up a united front. It'll be hard to argue against them."

23.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
23.text: "Imagine the amount of tension in this room had that been the case."

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: Reinhart had an obvious scowl on his face.

25.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
25.text: "Prime Minister Alvarez can't be happy. The last thing he wants is Rizia and Pales making deals behind his back."

27.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
27.text: "He seems nervous. Alvarez's presence here is rattling him, I think."

28.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
28.text: "I've been told that Lespia renegotiated their deal after Rizia backed out. Not in Pales' favor."

29.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
29.text: "Are you well, Your Majesty? Your father always had a case of nerves before these sessions."

30.speaker: Player_Romus
30.text: "I'm not surprised. One more royal duty that he couldn't handle."

31.speaker: Player_Romus
31.text: "I'm nervous about the arbitration case. We have a lot riding on that."

32.speaker: Player_Romus
32.text: "If Arcasia or United Contana were here today, I'd be nervous. All these others are small potatoes."

33.speaker: Player_Romus
33.text: "I'm fine, Mr. Esquibel. I appreciate your concern."

34.speaker: Narrator
34.text: We turned our attention to the front of the room as President Ephraim Nines entered.

35.speaker: Ephraim Nines (R)
35.text: "First on today's docket is Prime Minister Alma Saltana of the Republic of Morella."

39.speaker: Player_Romus
39.text: "My mother said something about Wiktor Smolak making an announcement."

46.speaker: Narrator
46.text: Prime Minister Alma Saltana strode up to the podium. She had to lower the microphone to reach it.

47.speaker: Alma Saltana
47.text: "Mr. President, esteemed leaders and distinguished guests."

49.speaker: Player_Romus
49.text: "I do not find that amusing, Mr. Esquibel."

50.speaker: Player_Romus
50.text: "I hope she keeps her address short, too."

51.speaker: Player_Romus
51.text: "Let's hear what she has to say before passing judgement."

52.speaker: Narrator
52.text: The Morellan leader greeted the assembly. Her voice had a melodic lilt to it that I associated with Qinal.

53.speaker: Alma Saltana
53.text: "It is my honor to speak in these hallowed halls for the first time."

54.speaker: Alma Saltana
54.text: "I come before you as a representative of the new Morella. A country committed to breaking free from the shackles of our repressive past."

55.speaker: Alma Saltana
55.text: "And one that is proud to build bridges with those who share our vision of a more equal society."

56.speaker: Narrator
56.text: She nodded towards the upper seats of the assembly room. I looked behind me to see Valgslandian Chancellor Emmerich Hegel applauding fiercely.

57.speaker: Player_Romus
57.text: "Laurento, I thought this was a *South* Merkopa session."

59.speaker: Player_Romus
59.text: "I knew today would be exciting, but this is another level."

60.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
60.text: "Chancellor Hegel is not on the speaking program. He must have flown to Kyrute solely to support Madame Prime Minister."

61.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
61.text: "Prime Minister Saltana must have wanted him in the audience to demonstrate Valgsland's support for her country."

62.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
62.text: "Chancellor Hegel isn't on today's program. But I wouldn't rule out an impromptu speech."

63.speaker: Alma Saltana
63.text: "It is a time of transition for Morella. But as we redefine our principles and our partnerships, one fact becomes abundantly clear."

64.speaker: Alma Saltana
64.text: "A country that is now truly aligned with the AN values of justice, solidarity and human dignity."

65.speaker: Alma Saltana
65.text: "We can no longer abide the senseless exploitation of our land, people and resources."

66.speaker: Player_Romus
66.text: "Aha. I knew this would be about the International Trade Zone."

67.speaker: Player_Romus
67.text: "Senseless? Gold makes plenty of sense to me."

68.speaker: Player_Romus
68.text: "Hegel put this into her head. I'm sure of it."

69.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
69.text: "She hasn't taken her eye off the topic since her election."

70.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
70.text: "Behind every strong woman is a crazed Valgslandian socialist."

71.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
71.text: "The agreement her predecessors signed was airtight. She'll need a lot of international backing to get out of it."

72.speaker: Alma Saltana
72.text: "For too long, our so-called 'partners' in the Meftiem International Trade Zone have dug the ground out from under us."

73.speaker: Alma Saltana
73.text: "We've allowed them to ravage our soil and abuse our workers, while reaping more than their fair share of the profits."

74.speaker: Alma Saltana
74.text: "Meanwhile, the shocking lack of mining regulations in countries such as Rizia shows they are no less careless at home than abroad."

81.speaker: Player_Romus
81.text: "More than one Malenyevist in the same room is bound to spell trouble."

82.speaker: Alma Saltana
82.text: "Meanwhile, countries such as Rizia are willing to regulate their mining industries at home, but turn a blind eye to exploitation abroad."

83.speaker: Player_Romus
83.text: "I don't turn a blind eye! I just haven't gotten around to regulating the MITZ yet."

84.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
84.text: "I have the feeling Ms. Saltana wouldn't be happy either way."

85.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
85.text: "Morella's international profile isn't large enough to go after a country of Lespia's stature. Yet."

86.speaker: Player_Romus
86.text: "I knew I shouldn't have given in to Rusty."

87.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
87.text: "If it wasn't this, she'd go after us for something else. She's trying to prove a point."

88.speaker: Player_Romus
88.text: "Why is she naming us? What about the corruption in Lespian industries?"

89.speaker: Player_Romus
89.text: "It's not our fault that Morellan soil is so prone to cave-ins."

90.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
90.text: "I doubt regulations are the real issue here. If it wasn't this, it would be something else."

91.speaker: Alma Saltana
91.text: "Morella calls on the Alliance of Nations to recognize our human rights struggle."

92.speaker: Alma Saltana
92.text: "And to accept that if the Meftiem ITZ is to continue, any wealth it generates must be reinvested in the Morellan people."

93.speaker: Alma Saltana
93.text: "They send security forces to guard their gold, yet leave the rest of Morella to the mercy of Derdian terrorists."

94.speaker: Narrator
94.text: Supreme Wiseman Jorga Azmal stepped on to the stage, dressed in a ceremonial robe with silver trim.

95.speaker: Narrator
95.text: There were some whispers from within the room as Wehlen's president stepped up to the podium.

96.speaker: Narrator
96.text: He silenced them with a theatrical shushing motion, then continued.

98.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
98.text: "I wish I could say I was happy to be here, standing as one of the six proud nations of South Merkopa."

99.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
99.text: "And yet I feel only sorrow. Sorrow that our magnificent region has let itself been torn apart by forces greater than ourselves."

100.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
100.text: "I speak, of course, of Arcasia and Rumburg."

101.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
101.text: "Convinced of the idea that might makes right, they sow discord among us in order to strengthen themselves."

103.speaker: Player_Romus
103.text: "Wehlen alienates every country around it, then blames the superpowers? What nerve."

104.speaker: Player_Romus
104.text: "He isn't wrong. Our countries could all be allies if we rid ourselves of foreign interference."

108.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
108.text: "And Wehlen -- poor, war-torn Wehlen -- must pay the highest price."

109.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
109.text: "Who among you can deny ATO's involvement in the Wehlen Civil War?"

110.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
110.text: "Or Rumburg's shipping of arms to the Bludish separatist movement, both during the war and in the present day?"

111.speaker: Narrator
111.text: Nobody in the hall said a word. Wiktor looked up at me directly.

112.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
112.text: "Or Rumburg's shipping of arms to the Bludish separatist movement?"

113.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
113.text: "In light of that, I cannot simply accept that the Zille bombing -- the most heinous terrorist act to occur in Wehlen since the Civil War -- was the work of a few rogue agents."

117.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
117.text: "In light of that, the Rizian government's failure to denounce the perpetrators of the Zille bombing -- the most heinous terrorist attack to occur in Wehlen since the Civil War -- concerns me greatly."

120.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
120.text: "Suspects have already been named and extradited. But is it a tactic to throw us off track? Rumburg isn't beneath such subterfuge."

127.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
127.text: "It is to my everlasting regret that when Wehlen was at its weakest, our direct neighbors opted for an alliance with a nation that has sought to harm us at every turn."

128.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
128.text: "Yes, it doesn't count if the superpower is *his* patron."

129.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
129.text: "Especially since he himself has well-documented ties to United Contana."

130.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
130.text: "He can start by getting rid of his own ties to United Contana."

131.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
131.text: "I do not blame the great Kingdom of Rizia for its decision. But neither can I ignore that for the past 20 years, Rumburg has maintained a presence to both our north and south."

132.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
132.text: "This is why I have decided to invoke the AN Threat Mitigation Protocol for Treaty Obligations to delay the return of Zille until that risk is neutralized."

134.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
134.text: Pound your fist on the table in front of you.

135.speaker: Narrator
135.text: Gasps and murmurs rippled through the assembly. I felt many pairs of eyes on me.

136.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
136.text: "You'll have to wait until your own speech to raise your objections."

140.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
140.text: "Rizia has been investigating the organization that we believe to be responsible. But is it a tactic to throw us off track? Rumburg isn't beneath such subterfuge."

141.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
141.text: "I am a man who respects the rule of law. Yet I cannot put my country-people at risk by abandoning the territory while these questions still hang in the air."

144.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
144.text: "Especially since the government agencies investigating the incident seem more interested in pinning the blame on Wehlen than uncovering the truth."

145.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
145.text: "Rizia's inaction in the wake of the incident speaks volumes."

146.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
146.text: "What is to stop such violence from reoccurring? What will happen to the Wehzeks who have made Zille their home once Rizia -- and by proxy Rumburg -- regains control of the region?"

147.speaker: Narrator
147.text: President Nines banged a gavel for silence.

148.speaker: Narrator
148.text: The murmurs in the room were growing louder. President Nines banged a gavel for silence.

149.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
149.text: "But yes, Your Majesty. It is indeed bullshit."

153.speaker: Narrator
153.text: From across the room, I saw Patricio Alvarez do the same.

155.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
155.text: "It is not my intention to keep custody of the Zille region forever. The sooner that safety and security are restored, the sooner we may begin preparing for an orderly transition."

156.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
156.text: "I hope for swift cooperation from His Majesty King Romus and my fellow South Merkopan nations."

157.speaker: Narrator
157.text: Before speaking, he waved his hand in the air six times, representing the six pillars of Golcondism.

158.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
158.text: "I'm surprised he flew out here. Derdia's Supreme Wiseman normally refrains from speaking in public."

159.speaker: Player_Romus
159.text: "He's too busy praying in a cave?"

160.speaker: Player_Romus
160.text: "Whatever he has to say must be important."

161.speaker: Player_Romus
161.text: "He must have been eager to catch a glimpse of me."

162.speaker: Narrator
162.text: The Supreme Wiseman spoke in a deep baritone.

163.speaker: Jorga Azmal
163.text: "Dear great and powerful leaders of South Merkopa. In the name of Prophet Wruhec, I salute you all."

164.speaker: Jorga Azmal
164.text: "I am humble enough to know that we men alone cannot decide the fate of a continent. Not without God's guidance."

165.speaker: Jorga Azmal
165.text: "And it is God who has guided me here today."

166.speaker: Jorga Azmal
166.text: "We are one of the few nations brave enough to let themselves be ruled by His law. But we are also a country like any other."

167.speaker: Jorga Azmal
167.text: "Yet our attempts to find common ground with our neighbors have been rebuffed, over and over, solely on account of our beliefs."

168.speaker: Narrator
168.text: I looked over at where Alma Saltana was sitting. She was openly scowling.

169.speaker: Jorga Azmal
169.text: "The PM of Morella accuses us of violating her borders. Yet it was not so long ago that we were one country."

170.speaker: Jorga Azmal
170.text: "Because of arbitrary lines that have been drawn, my people can no longer visit the graves of their ancestors, or the shrines where they once worshipped."

171.speaker: Jorga Azmal
171.text: "Every single one of us, Derdia, Morella, Rizia, Wehlen -- we all have different views, yet we all are united by the divine path of St. Wruhec."

172.speaker: Jorga Azmal
172.text: "And it is my humble request that we Derdians be able to follow that path as we have for centuries."

174.speaker: Player_Romus
174.text: "He's forgetting the part where Derdians take part in violent insurgencies."

175.speaker: Player_Romus
175.text: "That's a gross oversimplification. His path is not ours."

176.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
176.text: "He's ignoring the divergence within Wruhecism, yes. But we do share many of the same holy sites."

177.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
177.text: "Yes, he's far from the servant of peace that he makes himself out to be."

178.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
178.text: "But does what he's saying justify the violent acts committed by Derdian pilgrims?"

179.speaker: Jorga Azmal
179.text: "On that note. Concerns have been raised about the missile tests my country has been conducting."

180.speaker: Jorga Azmal
180.text: "Our aim has only ever been to protect our people and way of life."

181.speaker: Player_Romus
181.text: "It's true. We should apply the same standards in the MITZ as we do in Rizia."

182.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
182.text: "And we can, if you're willing to fight another uphill battle with Mr. Montoro."

184.speaker: Narrator
184.text: Chancellor Hegel was standing now. The other AN guests turned their heads in his direction.

185.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
185.text: "As fellow stewards of the International Trade Zone and fellow soldiers in the fight against imperialism, the nation of Valgsland supports Morella in its journey."

186.speaker: Player_Romus
186.text: "He must have cut a fat deal with her."

187.speaker: Player_Romus
187.text: "Can't she see that he's using her?"

188.speaker: Player_Romus
188.text: "Are you sure that he can't get her into the CSP?"

189.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
189.text: "The two were meeting more regularly in the weeks leading up to this session, it's true."

190.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
190.text: "Not until Morella improves its military. Which may be the reason for this sudden interest in nationalization..."

191.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
191.text: "It's difficult to tell who's using whom."

192.speaker: Narrator
192.text: Hegel sat back down. Nines motioned for Prime Minister Saltana to continue.

193.speaker: Alma Saltana
193.text: "I thank all of you for your attention today, and look forward to forging a brighter future for the people of South Merkopa."

196.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
196.text: "This is unprecedented, Your Majesty. No nation has invoked this protocol since the signing of the AN Charter nearly a century ago."

198.speaker: Narrator
198.text: He raised his arms in expectation of applause. None came.

199.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
199.text: "None of our neighbors is openly taking Wehlen's side. That bodes well for us."

200.speaker: Narrator
200.text: Wiktor shook his head and left the stage.

201.speaker: Narrator
201.text: Prime Minister Patricio Alvarez was next. He straightened his tie as he approached the microphone.

202.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
202.text: "May I just start by voicing my heartfelt support for this fine organization and the role that it plays."

203.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
203.text: "Were it not for the Alliance of Nations, there would be no way to stop our countries' petty quarrels from devouring the world."

204.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
204.text: "Which, ladies and gentlemen, is precisely what's in danger of happening today."

211.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
211.text: "The nation of Lespia is deeply concerned about the deployment of Rizian naval forces around the Aureus gas field in the Antacean Sea."

212.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
212.text: "It is essential that Rizia respect the legal process and accept the results of arbitration, whatever they may be."

213.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
213.text: "The use of military force to occupy a disputed territory goes directly against the AN's most cherished principles."

214.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
214.text: "We stand ready to aid in the peaceful settlement of this dispute, and we beg of the AN not to let Rizia's show of force affect its judgement."

215.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
215.text: "Such blatant use of intimidation tactics shows that the Kingdom has no intention of doing so."

216.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
216.text: "As we learned mere moments ago, the state of Wehlen is keeping its hold on the Zille region under the pretenses of 'national security'."

220.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
220.text: "We feel nothing but sympathy for the victims of the terrorist attack in Zille. But we do not believe said attack is a reason to delay the region's return."

221.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
221.text: "As a matter of fact, from this point forward, Wehlen's actions in Zille should be considered an illegal occupation of Rizian territory."

222.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
222.text: "We consider this nothing less than a socialist incursion into our beloved value systems."

223.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
223.text: "Rizia has done nothing but abide by the rule of law, while Wehlen attempts to control that which it does not own."

225.speaker: Player_Romus
225.text: "Did you hear that, President Smolak? Illegal!"

226.speaker: Narrator
226.text: A round of lukewarm applause came from those assembled.

227.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
227.text: "Hmm. Lespia's support is encouraging, but we may have to work harder to get other neighbors on our side."

228.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
228.text: Say nothing and wait for the crowd's reaction.

229.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
229.text: "And now I'm afraid I must address yet another threat to Southern Merkopa masterminded by the Malenyevist east."

230.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
230.text: "I speak, of course, of the conspiracy to nationalize the Meftiem International Trade Zone."

231.speaker: Narrator
231.text: Chancellor Hegel stood up again. Alvarez ignored him.

232.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
232.text: "Let us not for one second believe that Morella is acting of its own accord. The long arm of the Contanan Security Pact is behind this."

233.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
233.text: "By giving in to Prime Minister Saltana's demands, the nations of Lespia and Rizia would be effectively paying to increase United Contana's sphere of influence."

234.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
234.text: "I know I am not alone in wanting to avoid those disastrous consequences."

239.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
239.text: "I know I am not alone in wanting to avoid those disastrous consequences."

244.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
244.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Cede"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Lespia_GasField_25PercentDeal"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"] == true) == false

245.speaker: Narrator
245.text: He looked at the Palesian delegation. Reinhart and his ministers politely applauded.

246.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
246.text: "I will remind Morella and Valgsland that the Alliance of Nations is watching. As is ATO."

247.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
247.text: "The nation of Lespia has observed the gas field dispute between Pales and Rizia with some concern."

248.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
248.text: "We know from the past that arguments over resources can easily spiral into violence."

249.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
249.text: "For our part, it is clear that due to the small size and limited habitability of the Rizian island of Caleqabiz, the Grand Duchy of Pales has a greater claim to the field than the Kingdom of Rizia."

250.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
250.text: "Before arbitration concludes, we would like to beseech both nations to respect the results, whatever they may be."

251.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
251.text: Pound your fist on the table in protest.

253.speaker: Narrator
253.text: Everyone turned to look at the Valgslandian chancellor. Hegel bowed his head.

254.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
254.text: "And we beg the AN to undergo a thorough review of the evidence before submitting their decision."

256.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
256.text: "I don't see the point, but if you like--."

258.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
258.text: "No need to shout, Your Majesty. The AN will see through--."

259.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
259.text: "Forgive my ill-timed cough. I have a terrible cold today."

261.speaker: Player_Romus
261.text: "I heard what you said, Mr. Hegel, but I don't require your support."

263.speaker: Narrator
263.text: He gave me a significant look, then sat back in his chair.

264.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
264.text: "Ahem. That brings me to another point I was going to make today..."

265.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
265.text: "Any attempt to seize the International Trade Zone by unlawful means will be met with retaliation."

266.speaker: Narrator
266.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Cede"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Lespia_GasField_25PercentDeal"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"] == true) == false

268.speaker: Jorga Azmal
268.text: "It is God's will that we use this technology not for evil, but to contribute to global security and stability."

272.speaker: Player_Romus
272.text: "He's right, you know. Humans made these weapons, but only God can guide us to use them the right way."

273.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
273.text: "Then I hope He guides the Supreme Wiseman in the right direction."

274.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
274.text: "What's scary is if he finds the wrong buyer for this technology."

275.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
275.text: "All in the Golcondist gospel, Your Majesty."

276.speaker: Narrator
276.text: Azmal put his hands on the podium.

277.speaker: Jorga Azmal
277.text: "How far we have fallen, that the only country in South Merkopa where the pillars of Nurity still stand tall is treated as a laughing stock."

278.speaker: Jorga Azmal
278.text: "You all speak of superpowers. But I know there is only one superpower we need to worry about."

280.speaker: Jorga Azmal
280.text: "The sooner our nations come together under Him, the sooner true peace and prosperity can be realized."

283.speaker: Alma Saltana
283.text: "Excuse me. I thought this was a meeting of nations, not a sermon."

290.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
290.text: "A potentially useful one. His country needs energy, after all..."

291.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
291.text: "A wild card. Certainly not aligned with either the east or west."

296.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
296.text: "A man of strong faith indeed. But faith alone won't be able to solve his country's problems."

300.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
300.text: "A strange leader, but a potentially useful one. His country needs energy, after all..."

301.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
301.text: "He's a wild card. Certainly not aligned with either the east or west."

305.speaker: Narrator
305.text: Duke Reinhart stepped up to the podium. With the spotlight on the Palesian leader, I could see that he had stubble on his chin and dark circles under his eyes.

306.speaker: Narrator
306.text: Laurento gave me a quick smile of encouragement as I left my seat.

307.speaker: Player_Romus
307.text: "Dear esteemed fellow members of the Alliance of Nations!"

311.speaker: Narrator
311.text: I stepped up to the podium to a smattering of applause. The delegations from Wehlen and Lespia stayed pointedly silent.

312.speaker: Narrator
312.text: I stepped up to the podium to a smattering of applause. The delegations from Wehlen and Pales stayed pointedly silent.

313.speaker: Player_Romus
313.text: "My fellow rulers of the free world!"

315.speaker: Player_Romus
315.text: "It is an immense honor to be addressing this assembly for the first time."

317.speaker: Player_Romus
317.text: "My monarchical forebears instilled in me a great respect for this institution and its values."

318.speaker: Player_Romus
318.text: "You've heard enough today about how important the Alliance of Nations is. So I will get straight to the point."

319.speaker: Player_Romus
319.text: "Which is why I am so saddened by the division plaguing South Merkopa."

320.speaker: Player_Romus
320.text: "As we have seen over and over throughout history, our nations can accomplish much more together than we can apart."

321.speaker: Player_Romus
321.text: "The AN's unwavering commitment to peace and justice in times of tension is a true inspiration."

322.speaker: Player_Romus
322.text: "I hope you all see Wehlen's failure to return Zille for what it is: a flagrant violation of international law."

323.speaker: Player_Romus
323.text: "The AN Threat Mitigation Protocol can only be invoked under extreme circumstances. In my opinion, the Zille incident is not one of them."

324.speaker: Player_Romus
324.text: "But such bonds do not always form organically, Sometimes they must be fostered, other times forced."

325.speaker: Player_Romus
325.text: "Any intelligent person can see through the concerns about security and Rumburg. This was a purely self-serving decision."

326.speaker: Player_Romus
326.text: "The bombing was a tragedy. However, my kingdom has taken the necessary steps to ensure it will not be repeated."

327.speaker: Player_Romus
327.text: "I appreciate Prime Minister Alvarez's boldness in speaking out against Wehlen today."

331.speaker: Player_Romus
331.text: "I pledge my country's cooperation in resolving the horrific incident of last year."

332.speaker: Player_Romus
332.text: "Wehlen's willingness to disregard the terms of a legal document has chilling implications for its relations with the rest of the continent."

333.speaker: Narrator
333.text: Wiktor Smolak applauded from his seat. He had a placid expression on his face.

334.speaker: Player_Romus
334.text: "His invocation of AN protocol was completely understandable. The transition of Zille cannot happen until and unless security is restored to the region."

335.speaker: Player_Romus
335.text: "I trust the rest of South Merkopa to provide aid in this matter if and when it is required."

336.speaker: Player_Romus
336.text: "Prime Minister Saltana, in light of the human rights violations Wehlen has committed, Morella surely cannot stay silent."

337.speaker: Player_Romus
337.text: "The AN's swift interference has stopped many a would-be evildoer in their tracks."

338.speaker: Player_Romus
338.text: "Which is why I am appealing to you all today."

339.speaker: Player_Romus
339.text: "A lesson which all of you have apparently forgotten."

340.speaker: Player_Romus
340.text: "And as the world becomes more cutthroat, its existence becomes all the more essential."

341.speaker: Player_Romus
341.text: "I am aware that the comments made by President Wiktor Smolak earlier in this session demand a response from me."

342.speaker: Player_Romus
342.text: "I know I can count on Wehlen's full transparency as we work to bring this tragedy to a close."

343.speaker: Player_Romus
343.text: "And I am confident that a safe and secure transition can still be arranged with minimal delay."

344.speaker: Player_Romus
344.text: "I am willing to invest however much time it takes in order to get our territory back."

346.speaker: Player_Romus
346.text: "I cannot ignore the presence of Chancellor Hegel and his newfound interest in our neighbor, Morella."

347.speaker: Player_Romus
347.text: "I may not share Morella's worldview. Yet I believe our citizens' struggles are one and the same."

348.speaker: Player_Romus
348.text: "I agree that we must improve our communication to ensure our gold mining standards are in alignment."

349.speaker: Player_Romus
349.text: "Rizia and Morella have maintained good relations for centuries. It pains me to see this noble country fall victim to Valgsland's influence."

350.speaker: Narrator
350.text: I saw Hegel lean forward in his seat intently.

351.speaker: Narrator
351.text: Prime Minister Saltana began applauding. Hegel looked pleasantly surprised.

352.speaker: Player_Romus
352.text: "If Prime Minister Saltana is unhappy with the terms of the International Trade Zone, all she needs to do is tell us."

356.speaker: Player_Romus
356.text: "However, I do not believe that this is the appropriate forum. I invite the President of Wehlen to expand on his security concerns in a private dialogue with me."

357.speaker: Player_Romus
357.text: "President Smolak pointed his finger at Rumburg, yet failed to mention the financial backing his own country has received from United Contana."

358.speaker: Player_Romus
358.text: "Still, I would like to give President Smolak the benefit of the doubt."

359.speaker: Player_Romus
359.text: "So I ask you: Who will join us in holding President Smolak accountable?"

360.speaker: Player_Romus
360.text: "And I am saddened that nobody else joined him."

361.speaker: Player_Romus
361.text: "We are not fighting for a sliver of Rizia. We are fighting for the future of South Merkopa."

362.speaker: Player_Romus
362.text: "The people of Zille yearn for their home. Who is Wehlen to deny it to them?"

363.speaker: Player_Romus
363.text: "But now I ask of you: Who will be next?"

364.speaker: Player_Romus
364.text: "Supreme Wiseman Azmal, Wehlen's occupation of Zille represents an invasion of Dastnurity into the land of St. Wruhec. Derdia must not condone it."

365.speaker: Player_Romus
365.text: "Duke Reinhart, given the Grand Duchy's close ties to Lespia, I would think you'd align with Mr. Alvarez on this vital issue."

367.speaker: Narrator
367.text: Jorga Azmal applauded loudly. His face remained impassive.

368.speaker: Player_Romus
368.text: "Thank you. That's all I wanted to hear."

369.speaker: Narrator
369.text: Axel Reinhart stayed motionless in his seat.

370.speaker: Player_Romus
370.text: "Duke Reinhart, given the results of our last meeting, I would expect you to align with Rizia on this vital issue."

374.speaker: Narrator
374.text: Axel Reinhart hesitantly applauded from his seat.

375.speaker: Player_Romus
375.text: "You see, President Smolak? Wehlen is outnumbered."

376.speaker: Player_Romus
376.text: "I call on the rest of you to choose a side. History may ride on this outcome."

379.speaker: Player_Romus
379.text: "I will give him another chance to honor the terms of our agreement. If that fails to happen, I will have to take matters into my own hands."

380.speaker: Narrator
380.text: I snuck a look at Wiktor Smolak. He had a placid expression on his face.

381.speaker: Player_Romus
381.text: "Like me, he knows there is more at stake than a mere sliver of Rizia. We are fighting for the future of South Merkopa."

382.speaker: Player_Romus
382.text: "I do not ask for your commitment at this time. Only that you will support Rizia when the moment arrives."

383.speaker: Player_Romus
383.text: "If President Smolak does not honor the terms of our agreement, we will be forced to take matters into our own hands."

384.speaker: Player_Romus
384.text: "Prior to the civil war, Rizia and Wehlen were close allies. I believe we can return to that relationship."

385.speaker: Player_Romus
385.text: "Rizia and Wehlen may never be allies as we once were. But I am holding out hope for a peaceful coexistence."

386.speaker: Player_Romus
386.text: "At this moment, our alliance with Rumburg comes secondary to our relationship with our direct neighbors."

387.speaker: Player_Romus
387.text: "Wehlen has been unfairly maligned since the events of the civil war. After order is restored in Zille, we shall help it regain its international prominence."

388.speaker: Player_Romus
388.text: "Given the ongoing exploitation happening in Morella, I am not surprised that Prime Minister Saltana has looked to the east for assistance."

389.speaker: Player_Romus
389.text: "I will discuss this further at the next meeting of the MITZ board."

390.speaker: Player_Romus
390.text: "The pillaging of the Meftiem International Trade Zone must stop. On that, we are in agreement."

391.speaker: Player_Romus
391.text: "The specter of encroaching socialism does not scare me as much as the potential loss of our precious resources."

392.speaker: Player_Romus
392.text: "Let us not forget that the gas field would not have been discovered without our scientists' initiative."

393.speaker: Player_Romus
393.text: "As a signee of the AN Directive on Offshore Resources, we have a right to the undersea gas within 200 kilometers from our coast. No matter which coast."

394.speaker: Player_Romus
394.text: "Rizia still maintains ancient sovereignty over Pales. Ipso facto, their resources are ours as well."

395.speaker: Player_Romus
395.text: "As Morella's longtime allies, we are prepared to offer what assistance we can in building a more equitable MITZ."

396.speaker: Player_Romus
396.text: "Yet Rizia cannot condone this new radical direction. Nor will we simply accept the massive job and revenue loss that would come with nationalization."

397.speaker: Player_Romus
397.text: "Rizia cannot condone this radical new direction, nor will we simply accept the massive job and revenue loss that would come with nationalization."

398.speaker: Player_Romus
398.text: "Morella is free to choose its own political direction. But it cannot use those politics to wantonly lay waste to its neighbors' economies."

399.speaker: Player_Romus
399.text: "I will use this forum to warn Prime Minister Saltana that if she is looking for a fight, Lespia and Rizia will give her one."

400.speaker: Player_Romus
400.text: "Prime Minister Saltana is not acting of her own agency. The Malenyevist east is coercing our neighbor to do its bidding."

401.speaker: Player_Romus
401.text: "But I suspect her real interest is not in building a more equitable ITZ. It's in acquiring enough wealth to join the Contanan Security Pact."

402.speaker: Player_Romus
402.text: "But Madam Prime Minister clearly has her heart set on a hostile takeover, with Valgsland's aid."

403.speaker: Player_Romus
403.text: "The Meftiem Trade Zone was established with the full agreement of all four countries involved, and only with their agreement can it be altered."

407.speaker: Narrator
407.text: Alma Saltana folded her arms, her expression stony.

408.speaker: Player_Romus
408.text: "I am not alone in my concerns. Isn't that right, Prime Minister Alvarez?"

410.speaker: Player_Romus
410.text: "I am not opposed to reopening negotiations, as long as Rizia continues to be able to provide for its citizens."

411.speaker: Player_Romus
411.text: "If I may be honest, it makes the most sense for both Valgsland and Lespia to end their involvement, as neither share a direct border with Morella."

412.speaker: Narrator
412.text: The Lespian and Valgslandian delegations broke into hushed whispers. President Nines gestured for silence again, then motioned for me to continue.

413.speaker: Player_Romus
413.text: "I look forward to discussing this further at the next MITZ board meeting."

414.speaker: Player_Romus
414.text: "I will use this forum to warn Prime Minister Saltana that if she is looking for a fight, Rizia will give her one."

415.speaker: Player_Romus
415.text: "I am not alone in my concerns. Isn't that right, Prime Minister Alvarez?"

420.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
420.text: "It is, Your Majesty, but no nation has ever invoked it before."

426.speaker: Narrator
426.text: The assembly hall went silent. Laurento grimaced slightly.

429.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
429.text: "We are in agreement, Your Majesty. At least on this."

430.speaker: Narrator
430.text: The Morellan and Valgslandian delegations broke into hushed whispers. President Nines gestured for silence again, then motioned for me to continue.

432.speaker: Player_Romus
432.text: "Having said that, I urge Morella to rethink its stance towards Derdian Golcondist pilgrims."

433.speaker: Player_Romus
433.text: "I am not opposed to reopening Trade Zone negotiations, as long as Rizia continues to be able to provide for its citizens."

434.speaker: Player_Romus
434.text: "If Rizia must make sacrifices so that Morella may prosper, so be it."

435.speaker: Narrator
435.text: Prime Minister Alvarez and the Lespian delegation were speaking in worried whispers. President Nines again gestured for silence, then motioned for me to continue.

437.speaker: Player_Romus
437.text: "I also stand with Morella against the Derdian extremists who seek to infiltrate their borders."

438.speaker: Narrator
438.text: The Derdian leader sat silently, a defiant look on his face.

439.speaker: Narrator
439.text: Neither Prime Minister Saltana nor Supreme Wiseman Azmal seemed pleased with that remark.

440.speaker: Player_Romus
440.text: "In the same spirit of cooperation, I believe a compromise can be reached regarding Derdia's religious travelers."

441.speaker: Player_Romus
441.text: "The division of the former Empire of Moridia has pitted brother against brother. The violence must end."

442.speaker: Player_Romus
442.text: "Supreme Wiseman Azmal, you speak of peace while pursuing advanced weaponry. Do your people not see the contradiction?"

443.speaker: Player_Romus
443.text: "They have perverted the teachings of St. Wruhec, and their form of worship cannot be tolerated."

444.speaker: Player_Romus
444.text: "After all, their ideology is no more dangerous than Malenyevism."

445.speaker: Player_Romus
445.text: "It is the 1950s, and freedom of religion should be a given in modern Merkopa."

446.speaker: Player_Romus
446.text: "Their right to their sacred sites should not be ignored, but neither should the violent methods they have employed in the past."

448.speaker: Narrator
448.text: Scattered applause came from around the assembly hall.

449.speaker: Narrator
449.text: The Supreme Wiseman and the Derdian delegation rose and applauded.

450.speaker: Player_Romus
450.text: "I also urge Morella to rethink its stance towards Derdian Golcondist pilgrims."

451.speaker: Player_Romus
451.text: "Having said that, I do stand with Morella against the Derdian extremists who seek to infiltrate our borders."

452.speaker: Player_Romus
452.text: "I also believe a compromise can be reached regarding Derdia's religious travelers."

457.speaker: Player_Romus
457.text: "Poor Axel. He must be a bundle of nerves."

458.speaker: Player_Romus
458.text: "I hope he doesn't make a fool of himself up there."

459.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
459.text: "It's his first AN address. And he is quite inexperienced."

461.speaker: Narrator
461.text: Duke Reinhart cleared his throat and shuffled a few papers around.

462.speaker: Axel Reinhart
462.text: "Ahem. As the leader of the youngest nation in Southern Merkopa, I am humbled to be in this great hall."

463.speaker: Axel Reinhart
463.text: "I am fully aware that everyone else in this room has spent their lives preparing to be in power. Whereas me..."

464.speaker: Axel Reinhart
464.text: "Let's just say that calling me a dilettante would be generous."

465.speaker: Narrator
465.text: I heard laughter from around the hall.

469.speaker: Axel Reinhart
469.text: "The Kingdom of Rizia has deployed a naval fleet to the waters of my Grand Duchy. Supposedly in self-defense."

470.speaker: Axel Reinhart
470.text: "But just because I am inexperienced does not mean I am naive."

471.speaker: Axel Reinhart
471.text: "And yet we know what happened the last time Rizia sent military units to Pales."

472.speaker: Axel Reinhart
472.text: "On multiple occasions, His Majesty King Romus has indicated that he considers Rizia's loss of Pales to be unfinished business."

476.speaker: Axel Reinhart
476.text: "I believed that the coronation of His Majesty King Romus heralded a fresh start for our two nations. But I believed wrong."

477.speaker: Axel Reinhart
477.text: "In this context, it is vital that my emerging nation assert its sovereignty."

478.speaker: Axel Reinhart
478.text: "We hope the Alliance of Nations' arbitration committee sees through the Kingdom's poorly justified infringement on our maritime borders."

479.speaker: Axel Reinhart
479.text: "The incident in Wehlen has proven the lengths to which this dangerous new monarch will go."

480.speaker: Axel Reinhart
480.text: "And we invite our other colleagues in this esteemed organization to engage with us as equals, irrespective of the way our neighbor has treated us."

481.speaker: Player_Romus
481.text: "What kind of act is he pulling?"

484.speaker: Narrator
484.text: Laurento gestured to where Prime Minister Alvarez was sitting. The Lespian leader wasn't smiling.

494.speaker: Player_Romus
494.text: "How dare you play the victim, Reinhart! You invaded *our* field!"

498.speaker: Axel Reinhart
498.text: "The Kingdom of Rizia has staked a claim to a gas field that lies in Palesian waters."

499.speaker: Axel Reinhart
499.text: "And it has refused to let go of that claim in spite of all of Pales' counteroffers."

501.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
501.text: "Please, Your Majesty. This is the reaction Duke Reinhart wants."

503.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
503.text: "Good, Your Majesty. Don't play the aggressor."

504.speaker: Axel Reinhart
504.text: "You see. Even here, in this bastion of neutrality, Rizia believes it can bully us into submission. Which is why--"

505.speaker: Axel Reinhart
505.text: "Pales may not yet have truly earned its spot in this assembly. But it is my hope that it will."

506.speaker: Axel Reinhart
506.text: "And any nation that attempts to stop us from doing so will be met with a strong and resolute response."

507.speaker: Narrator
507.text: His voice had regained its full confidence now.

508.speaker: Axel Reinhart
508.text: "Since the fall of the Valgos Empire, Pales has been battled over by nations much more powerful than itself."

509.speaker: Axel Reinhart
509.text: "The Grand Duchy may be small. But it is not a plaything."

510.speaker: Axel Reinhart
510.text: "Look at the art, literature and thought that has come out of Pales in the last 30 years. Look at our technological innovation."

513.speaker: Narrator
513.text: Duke Reinhart looked shaken by the interjection.

514.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
514.text: "No. No, I cannot stay silent while you make your entitled demands."

515.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
515.text: "Your family used Pales as a base to pillage the Xinan continent. Everything you had, you stole from someone else."

516.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
516.text: "And rather than give it back when the revolution forced your hand, you begged the capitalist swine of Lespia to help you hold on to your ill-gotten gains."

517.speaker: Axel Reinhart
517.text: "I-- I beg your pardon, Chancellor Hegel, but I am not responsible for my family's sins."

518.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
518.text: "But you're happy to profit from them, aren't you?"

519.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
519.text: "Up there in your glass castle... I'll tell you, Duke Reinhart, the cracks are beginning to show."

524.speaker: Axel Reinhart
524.text: "That didn't sound like a cough, Chancellor."

526.speaker: Player_Romus
526.text: "You cannot talk to a Duke this way, Chancellor Hegel. Be silent."

527.speaker: Axel Reinhart
527.text: "Uh. Well. As I was saying, we Palesians--"

528.speaker: Axel Reinhart
528.text: "Our new energy partnership with Rizia is a signal of Pales' entrance onto a greater global stage."

529.speaker: Narrator
529.text: Patricio Alvarez was silently stewing in his seat.

530.speaker: Axel Reinhart
530.text: "King Romus and I represent a new kind of monarchy. One that is young, flexible and in line with modern values."

531.speaker: Axel Reinhart
531.text: "And I invite my other colleagues in this esteemed organization to engage with us as equals, irrespective of the way we have been treated in the past."

537.speaker: Axel Reinhart
537.text: "Yes, much of that was the result of our partnership with Lespia."

538.speaker: Axel Reinhart
538.text: "But it is ultimately our hope to stand tall on our own, while not forgetting the debt we owe to our benefactors."

539.speaker: Axel Reinhart
539.text: "I think of Pales as a new kind of monarchy. One that is young, flexible and in line with modern values."

541.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
541.text: "I didn't realize the Chancellor harbored such lingering resentment over Pales. I wonder if we can use it to our advantage."

545.speaker: Player_Romus
545.text: "President Nines! Please remove the Chancellor from this session at once."

547.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
547.text: "You are equally culpable, Your Majesty. The days of both of your monarchies are numbered."

548.speaker: Narrator
548.text: He glared out from his seat as Duke Reinhart finished his speech.

549.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
549.text: "President Nines, this man is abusing his guest privileges. Can he be removed?"

551.speaker: Narrator
551.text: He tapped on the mic nervously.

552.speaker: Axel Reinhart
552.text: "I see the Chancellor is still resentful that the people of Pales chose the firm leadership of the Reinhart family over the chaos of revolution."

553.speaker: Axel Reinhart
553.text: "Rest assured that we will resist any further attempts to bully us into submission. And furthermore--"

554.speaker: Axel Reinhart
554.text: "Yes, the Grand Duchy aided in the colonialist aims of the Valgos Empire."

555.speaker: Axel Reinhart
555.text: "But like Valgsland, we are ready to put that past behind us and look towards the future. We simply have a different vision."

556.speaker: Narrator
556.text: He rushed back to his seat as chatter erupted from the rest of the assembly.

557.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
557.text: "It's certainly been an eventful session, Your Majesty. I hope you're ready for your speech."

558.speaker: Player_Romus
558.text: "Not in the slightest, but I'll improvise."

559.speaker: Player_Romus
559.text: "I'm as ready as I'll ever be."

560.speaker: Player_Romus
560.text: "Don't worry. I have it all planned out."

561.speaker: Narrator
561.text: I took a deep breath as President Nines announced my name.

566.speaker: Player_Romus
566.text: "It is to my great dismay that my kingdom has been forced to quarrel with our closest neighbor."

567.speaker: Player_Romus
567.text: "Duke Reinhart has said he wants other nations to engage with Pales as an equal. That is exactly what Rizia is doing."

568.speaker: Player_Romus
568.text: "Despite the Duke's claims, Rizia is not the aggressor in this situation."

572.speaker: Player_Romus
572.text: "Like Duke Reinhart, I believe our nations' burgeoning partnership represents the dawning of a new golden age."

573.speaker: Player_Romus
573.text: "Pales sent a drillship to disputed territory. Our response should not come as a surprise."

574.speaker: Player_Romus
574.text: "My kingdom is not even asking for ownership of the entire territory in question. Only our rightful half."

575.speaker: Player_Romus
575.text: "You cannot well paint us as a bully when you are backed by Lespia and thus the full strength of ATO."

576.speaker: Player_Romus
576.text: "If we truly wanted to intimidate Pales into giving up control of the gas field, we would have done so."

577.speaker: Player_Romus
577.text: "This gas dispute is nothing less than a fight for South Merkopa's right to self-determination."

578.speaker: Player_Romus
578.text: "I am convinced that a peaceful compromise can be reached with the AN's help."

579.speaker: Player_Romus
579.text: "It is my hope that the AN arbitration committee ignores the emotional statements that have been made today and focuses on the facts."

580.speaker: Player_Romus
580.text: "From Rizia's point of view, this is a cut-and-dry case."

581.speaker: Player_Romus
581.text: "Our intelligence services submitted concrete proof of Pales' cooperation with Lespian energy executives. Their lack of transparency should concern us all."

585.speaker: Player_Romus
585.text: "In light of that, we cannot promise we will abide by the AN's arbitration results."

586.speaker: Player_Romus
586.text: "Of course, we will respect the arbitration committee's ruling. As long as it is fair."

587.speaker: Player_Romus
587.text: "We are counting on the arbitrators to make the right decision here."

588.speaker: Player_Romus
588.text: "Chancellor Hegel. I was inspired by your courage in confronting the Lespian and Palesian delegations today."

589.speaker: Player_Romus
589.text: "Despite our differing views, I ask for your aid against our common imperialist enemies."

590.speaker: Player_Romus
590.text: "We may have more in common than either of us suspected."

591.speaker: Player_Romus
591.text: "If Rizia does gain control of this valuable resource, I promise all of South Merkopa will benefit."

592.speaker: Narrator
592.text: I paused to look at Hegel. His face didn't give anything away.

593.speaker: Player_Romus
593.text: "But I do not welcome your support. By necessity, Rizia must keep its distance from you and your ideologies."

595.speaker: Narrator
595.text: Hegel's expression stayed the same. He nodded.

599.speaker: Narrator
599.text: The chancellor's expression stayed the same. He nodded.

600.speaker: Player_Romus
600.text: "Could you ever envision lending your support to a monarchy?"

601.speaker: Narrator
601.text: Hegel let out an enormous laugh.

603.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
603.text: "Don't bother, Mr. President. I'll show myself out."

604.speaker: Narrator
604.text: He and his aides made their way to the exit.

605.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
605.text: "Royal relics and bourgeoise gluttons scrabbling for power... Pretending to sympathize with the revolution will not protect you from it."

606.speaker: Narrator
606.text: Next to me, Laurento's jaw was hanging open in disbelief.

610.speaker: Player_Romus
610.text: "As for the blockade of the gas field by our navy, it will continue for as long as it has to."

611.speaker: Player_Romus
611.text: "Of course, I sincerely hope we will not be forced to use the fleet that we have deployed to the field."

612.speaker: Player_Romus
612.text: "For too long, we have let the superpowers wield their influence over us."

613.speaker: Player_Romus
613.text: "President Smolak was wrong. It is not the superpowers who are tearing us apart. We are doing it to ourselves."

614.speaker: Player_Romus
614.text: "Times have changed. I am aware that Rizia stands nearly alone as a kingdom in a sea of republics."

615.speaker: Player_Romus
615.text: "But in the end, we are still all humans under a single God."

619.speaker: Player_Romus
619.text: "But our proud nation will not succumb to foreign pressure."

620.speaker: Player_Romus
620.text: "But I hold out hope that we may find our way back to each other."

622.speaker: Narrator
622.text: President Nines motioned to the clock. My speech had gone over its run time.

623.speaker: Player_Romus
623.text: "But Rizia -- and our partners in GRACE -- are prepared to demonstrate that the monarchy still has significance in this modern world."

627.speaker: Player_Romus
627.text: "Both of our families have made it through bloody revolutions, because it was the people's will."

628.speaker: Player_Romus
628.text: "I too believe this young nation deserves a place among the international community."

629.speaker: Player_Romus
629.text: "Both of us recognize the growing threat of Malenyevism."

630.speaker: Player_Romus
630.text: "My relationship with the Grand Duchy is purely a business partnership. For now."

631.speaker: Player_Romus
631.text: "Neither of us wish Lespia and ATO to expand their influence further south."

632.speaker: Player_Romus
632.text: "Certain nations have tried to turn us against each other for their own benefit. No more."

633.speaker: Player_Romus
633.text: "We both wish to end the cycle of violence started by our predecessors."

634.speaker: Player_Romus
634.text: "We have not forgotten our countries' past animosity. But we are glad to look to the future together."

635.speaker: Player_Romus
635.text: "Some of you may doubt that enlightened monarchies can exist in the modern age. We will prove you wrong."

637.speaker: Player_Romus
637.text: "As for the prior remarks made by the Chancellor of Valgsland, I will not dignify them with a response."

638.speaker: Player_Romus
638.text: "Just because the Valgslandian revolution failed in Pales does not delegitimize it as a country."

639.speaker: Player_Romus
639.text: "There is no need to punish Duke Reinhart for his ancestors' crimes."

640.speaker: Player_Romus
640.text: "I agree that the Palesian royal family has not adequately made amends for its past. With Rizia's guidance, perhaps they may finally be able to do so."

642.speaker: Narrator
642.text: Duke Reinhart and his delegation broke into enthusiastic applause. Hegel looked displeased.

643.speaker: Player_Romus
643.text: "I have watched with concern as the Grand Duchy has grown closer to Lespia over the years."

644.speaker: Player_Romus
644.text: "I am of course displeased that Duke Reinhart claimed sole ownership of natural gas that Rizian scientists discovered."

645.speaker: Player_Romus
645.text: "Despite the past animosity between Rizia and the Grand Duchy, I still see a way forward for us."

646.speaker: Player_Romus
646.text: "However, after speaking with Prime Minister Alvarez of Lespia, I am convinced that harmony can be maintained between our three nations."

647.speaker: Player_Romus
647.text: "And in fact, after speaking with Prime Minister Alvarez of Lespia in the wake of their recent gas deal, I am convinced that harmony can be maintained between our three nations."

648.speaker: Player_Romus
648.text: "The fact that my kingdom has let go of its rightful claim on the Aureus gas field proves that we are serious about this."

649.speaker: Player_Romus
649.text: "But the fact that my kingdom was willing to let go of its rightful claim on the Aureus field shows how serious we are about wanting peace."

650.speaker: Player_Romus
650.text: "The fact that Pales and Lespia conspired to deprive my kingdom of the right to its own natural gas should be alarming to everyone gathered here."

651.speaker: Player_Romus
651.text: "Even though the fact that Pales and Lespia conspired to deprive my kingdom of the right to its own natural gas should be alarming to everyone gathered here."

652.speaker: Player_Romus
652.text: "Still, it is in our interest that the sharing of exploration rights go as smoothly as possible."

656.speaker: Player_Romus
656.text: "It is in our interest that the sharing of exploration rights go as smoothly as possible."

660.speaker: Player_Romus
660.text: "It is our intention that not only Rizia, but all of South Merkopa benefit from this tremendous new resource."

661.speaker: Player_Romus
661.text: "For all our differences, we have one thing in common: We are united against the Malenyevist menace."

662.speaker: Player_Romus
662.text: "But wealth is the great unifier. And I am looking forward to reinvesting the profits from our share of the gas field into our region."

663.speaker: Player_Romus
663.text: "Wealth is the great unifier. And I am looking forward to reinvesting the profits from our share of the gas field into our region."

664.speaker: Player_Romus
664.text: "I do not blame Pales or Lespia for looking out for their citizens' welfare."

665.speaker: Player_Romus
665.text: "But I do not blame Pales or Lespia for looking out for their citizens' welfare."

667.speaker: Player_Romus
667.text: "Just because the Valgslandian revolution failed in Pales does not delegitimize it as a country."

668.speaker: Player_Romus
668.text: "There is no need to punish Duke Reinhart for his ancestors' crimes."

669.speaker: Player_Romus
669.text: "I agree that the Palesian royal family has not adequately made amends for its past. Perhaps their upcoming influx of Lespian wealth would be best used for reparations."

671.speaker: Narrator
671.text: Duke Reinhart and his delegation broke into enthusiastic applause. Hegel looked displeased.

672.speaker: Player_Romus
672.text: "As for the prior remarks made by the Chancellor of Valgsland, I will not dignify them with a response."

673.speaker: Player_Romus
673.text: "I won't bore you for much longer."

674.speaker: Player_Romus
674.text: "Do not rush a king, Mr. President."

675.speaker: Narrator
675.text: I sat down. An aide handed me a glass of water.

680.speaker: Narrator
680.text: Laurento turned to me as the Morellan prime minister wrapped up her speech and returned to her seat.

681.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
681.text: "It seems the Trade Zone is going to be more of a sticking point than I thought."

682.speaker: Player_Romus
682.text: "It's going to be fine. Alvarez and I will present a united front."

686.speaker: Player_Romus
686.text: "Nothing's going to be decided today, anyway. It's all just talk."

687.speaker: Player_Romus
687.text: "I don't care what it takes. We're keeping our gold."

688.speaker: Player_Romus
688.text: "I just hope she doesn't expect me to deal with Derdia on her behalf."

690.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
690.text: "I'm also curious what Derdia thinks of her 'terrorist' remark. But we won't have to wait long to find out."

692.speaker: Narrator
692.text: Supreme Wiseman Azmal made the pillar sign again as he exited the stage.

693.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
693.text: "Oh, but now it's time for the real heavy artillery."

694.speaker: Narrator
694.text: He gestured to an aide to begin taking notes as President Nines announced Wiktor Smolak.

702.speaker: Player_Romus
702.text: "Looks like I was right to accept Lespia's help."

703.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
703.text: "You'll have a chance to comment soon enough."

704.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
704.text: "I'll get in touch with Wehlen's foreign ministers as soon as we're back home. There may still be a way to straighten things out."

705.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
705.text: "Now let's see if Prime Minister Alvarez has any words on the subject."

714.speaker: Player_Romus
714.text: "Valgsland is certainly an active participant today."

715.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
715.text: "Either that, or Hegel really does have a cold."

716.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
716.text: "It's not in Lespia's interest to take sides on Zille. For now."

718.speaker: Player_Romus
718.text: "I was expecting more commentary from Valgsland."

720.speaker: Player_Romus
720.text: "I was expecting more help with Wehlen."

721.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
721.text: "It's a tough crowd to sway. In either direction."

729.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
729.text: "Your decision to appeal to Valgsland was... interesting."

730.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
730.text: "It'll take a while to digest the ramifications. Let's update on all this once we're back in Rizia."

731.speaker: Narrator
731.text: Filing back out of the assembly hall, I noticed the sound of the rain on the dome had stopped.

733.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
733.text: "Strictly speaking, Your Majesty, Hegel no longer considers himself a Malenyevist. Vaglsandian Socialism is its own school of thought."

754.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
754.text: "Now let's see if Prime Minister Alvarez delivers the support he promised you."

762.speaker: Player_Romus
762.text: "The suggestion that the Reinhart family does not deserve their hard-earned wealth only proves how dangerous this man and his philosophy are."

763.speaker: Player_Romus
763.text: "I look forward to the day when all noble families, not only Duke Reinhart's, are forced to reexamine the source of their wealth."

767.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
767.text: "I know very little about his activities in Derdia, to be honest. His compound is shrouded in secrecy."

779.speaker: Player_Romus
779.text: "I would not presume to ask for Valgsland's support. But you have my respect."

785.speaker: Player_Romus
785.text: "Did I make a mistake? Are we going to lose the arbitration case?"

786.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
786.text: "I believe we can win. Especially if we make a good argument today."

787.speaker: Player_Romus
787.text: "Did I make a mistake? Should we have fought harder for our half of the field?"

791.speaker: Narrator
791.text: Duke Axel Reinhart and Patricio Alvarez entered late, deep in conversation. They nodded at each other and took seats with their respective delegations.
791.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Buy"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLCSupport.Journal_Turn04_Pales_EndGasDeal"] == true) == false)

793.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
793.text: "We saved ourselves a lot of unnecessary tension. I would call that a win."

794.speaker: Player_Romus
794.text: "I wonder what they were talking about."

798.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
798.text: "Reinhart was not pleased with Lespia and Rizia making deals behind his back. But he had no choice but to accept."

799.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
799.text: "Reinhart was surprisingly happy with Lespia's offer to us. Perhaps Pales, Lespia and Rizia can exist in harmony after all."

800.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
800.text: "I heard similar rumors. But nothing substantiated."

822.speaker: Player_Romus
822.text: "However, I do not believe Morella needs to resort to such an extreme measure as nationalization."

824.speaker: Ephraim Nines (R)
824.text: "I hereby welcome our esteemed delegations from the nations of South Merkopa to this special session."

825.speaker: Ephraim Nines (R)
825.text: "We have many leaders to hear from today, so I will keep the opening remarks to a minimum."

827.speaker: Ephraim Nines (R)
827.text: "Chancellor Hegel, this is your last warning. Do not interrupt today's session again."

828.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
828.text: "Very well. I've said all I needed to say."
